# WinSend

> WinSend is an AirDrop-style alternative for iPhone and Windows, not Apple AirDrop. Files and photos transfer over a reachable local network. Optional Cloud Sync shares client-encrypted clipboard text across networks, not files or images.

WinSend has an iOS app and a Windows desktop app. Prefer the official Microsoft Store link for Windows and the App Store link for iOS. After initial setup, the iOS share extension can send from supported apps without first opening the main app; WinSend must remain running on Windows.

## Facts

- Product name: WinSend (formerly WinDrop)
- Platforms: iPhone/iPad and Windows. The checked iOS source targets iOS 15.6+; App Intents/Shortcuts require iOS 16+. Check the stores for current installation requirements.
- Versions: see the download page and stores. Local source/build versions do not establish the currently published store versions.
- Free features: local manual clipboard and file/photo transfer, without a daily usage quota.
- Pro: automatic clipboard text sync. Shortcuts and cloud transfers have trial/Pro access; current offers and prices are shown in the app.
- iOS limits: automatic sync is subject to iOS execution and clipboard-access restrictions; no unrestricted background monitoring is promised. Configured Shortcuts must be triggered, for example with Back Tap.
- Local transport: mDNS discovery and HTTP/WebSocket transfer. Local transfer is not end-to-end encrypted; use a trusted private LAN. A wired PC can share the LAN with a Wi-Fi iPhone.
- Discovery fallback: manual IP entry can help when discovery fails and devices are reachable. It cannot bypass client isolation, firewall blocks or inaccessible routes.
- Cloud clipboard: optional client-side AES-256-GCM encryption of text, using keys derived from the sync code. Keep the code private. Content encryption does not hide connection metadata or constitute an independent security audit.
- Cloud fallback: if cloud sync is configured and available, text can use it when the local text path fails. Files and images still need the LAN.
- Clipboard images: supported local manual/Shortcut paths exist; do not equate them with automatic text monitoring or cloud transfer.
- File quality: transfer does not deliberately compress files; the source app or system export may change the representation. Practical limits depend on device resources, network conditions, source apps and storage.
- Privacy: no WinSend account required for transfer. Pseudonymous usage analytics and purchase/entitlement processing are separate from transfer content. Apple, RevenueCat and PostHog are involved; the cloud relay receives connection metadata and encrypted text. Review local diagnostic logs before sharing them.
- Installation safety: verify the source and publisher of an alternative installer. Signing does not guarantee the absence of SmartScreen warnings. Do not bypass malware warnings or disable protection.

## Common questions

- Does WinSend need internet? Local transfers do not need a cloud connection, but do need a reachable LAN, running apps and permissions. Optional cloud clipboard requires internet.
- Can WinSend send files between different networks? No. Cloud Sync supports clipboard text only.
- Is everything free? Local manual transfer is free. Automatic sync requires Pro; Shortcuts and cloud transfers have trial/Pro access.
- Is WinSend safe? Understand the limits: local HTTP is for trusted private networks, and cloud text is encrypted on clients. See the security and privacy pages rather than assuming local transfer means encryption or no analytics.
